traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.38, 0.3, 0.24], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.height_max_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922), as Rhizophora Mangle: a round-topped bushy tree usually 15 to 20 ft high (4.6 m to 6.1 m), occasionally 70 to 80 ft (21.3 m to 24.4 m). Small (1933, pp. 938-939) says becoming 20 m tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Rhizophora mangle (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.83 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 28 records in 13 sources); trunks 0.88, branches 0.69. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an evergreen tree of tropical coasts, 5 to 10 m tall, standing on a tangle of arching prop roots that leave the trunk and lower branches and reach down into the mud; glossy, leathery, opposite leaves and small pale yellow flowers. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 5 m at 20 years and 7 m at 50. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark glossy green leaves, grey-brown bark and roots. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth grey-brown bark with lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four whitish petals between four sepals, eight stamens and a half-inferior pistil of two carpels, from the characters of its own and Rhizophoraceae's by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: Little and Skolmen's Common Forest Trees of Hawaii, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read: sepals 4, narrow, pale yellow, almost 13 mm long, leathery and persistent; petals 4, narrow, about 10 mm, whitish, woolly inside; a two-celled ovary mostly inferior but conical at its apex. The New York Botanical Garden's account (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read) gives 8 stamens round the style.
